# Agent notes

## Shape

- Two entries, `src/index.ts` (server) and `src/tui.tsx` (terminal UI), each bundled to one self-contained file.
  `scripts/build.mjs` fails on a relative import or a non-host external.
- One status model (`src/status.ts`) feeds the dialog, `/voice-status`, the status RPC and `voice_status`.
- One dictation flow (`src/dictation/flow.ts`) and one pure state machine (`src/dictation/state.ts`).
- The engine is a pinned child process, never an in-process library: `aurum converse --stdio` for speech,
  `aurum record` for the microphone, `aurum play` for the speaker.

## Forbidden

- No `ctx.ui.slot` calls by default. The single opt-in footer row (`statusIndicator: "footer"`) is the documented S1
  exception; do not add another.
- No network call in status, dictation, read-aloud or the engine RPC. Only `/voice-install` downloads, and only from
  the pinned manifest.
- No transcript, audio, key or path outside the plugin cache in status, errors, logs or commands.
- No `dependencies`, `optionalDependencies`, host `peerDependencies`, `engines` or lifecycle scripts. The engine comes from
  the GitHub release, not from a package.
- Do not edit the shared part of `src/host/tools-rpc.ts` (outside its PLUGIN-SPECIFIC block) or
  `scripts/check-icons.mjs`; both are pinned by copy checks.
- Do not add a model provider, a cloud STT/TTS path or a second engine. Utilities owns file transcription.
- Releases come only from `.github/workflows/release.yml` ("Releasing" in [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md)). A
  release-prep PR sets `version` in `package.json` and the install specs and runs `node scripts/changelog.mjs release`;
  once it is on `master` and CI passed, run the `native` workflow on that commit
  (`gh workflow run native.yml --ref master`), then start the release with
  `gh workflow run release.yml --ref master -f sha=<its full sha> -f native_run=<the native run id>`. The workflow
  builds `dist/`, makes the release commit on a temporary `release/v<version>` branch, checks and stages everything, and
  waits for the owner to approve the `release` environment; only then does it create the tag `v<version>` and the GitHub
  Release. Never push a tag or a `release/*` branch, and never commit, tag or publish a release by hand. Agents never
  approve a release, never call the deployment-approval API, and never bypass a ruleset or the environment.
- No personal email in anything we publish. Every commit is authored and committed as
  `joe-broadhead <91376460+joe-broadhead@users.noreply.github.com>`, except the release commit and tag, which the
  release workflow makes as `github-actions[bot]`. Before committing or tagging, check that
  `git config user.email` is that address: a fresh clone inherits the machine's global identity, which is not that
  address. Never commit, tag or publish with a work or personal address, or with a local hostname.

## Checks

`npm run check` is the gate: `build`, `typecheck`, `unit`, `icons`, `copies`, `forbidden`, `evals`, `host` (each stock release
in `TESTED_HOSTS`), `pack` (the packed install, which carries no engine), `whitelist`
and `actionlint`. The tested hosts are tested on 2.2.3, 2.2.4, 2.2.5 and 2.2.6. `npm run stock:install` puts each stock release in
`.cache/stock`, and `OPENCODE_BIN_<version>` overrides one; with neither, the host stage says so and skips, and in CI a gap
is a failure. The eval pack's static tier (`node evals/check.mjs`) is part of the check.

# Voice

Local dictation and read-aloud, powered by Aurum. Audio stays on this machine; a recording is never kept.

## Check before you offer

Call `voice_status` before telling the user dictation is available. It reports the engine, the models, the microphone
permission and one next step. Do not claim any of them from memory or from an earlier call in the session: the engine
can be missing, a model can be absent, and the microphone can be denied.

- If the next step is `/voice-install`, say that models are missing and offer the command. Do not run a download
  yourself.
- If the microphone is denied, name System Settings → Privacy & Security → Microphone. Never suggest a workaround.
- If the engine is missing, say to run `/voice-install`. If it is unverified, say to run `/voice-install` again, which replaces it.

## Speak

`voice_speak` reads text aloud on the user's machine. Every tool runs without asking by default, so it just speaks; if
the user set `access: "ask-changes"` the approval is the yes, so do not ask in chat as well. Pass the text the user
asked for, up to 5,000 characters; a long reply is cut with `…`.

A refusal or a decline means nothing was spoken. Say that and offer the text instead.

Do not call `voice_speak` to "test" the voice, to read your own reasoning, or on every reply. Use it when the user asks
for it, or when `autoSpeak` is on, which the plugin handles itself.

## Dictation is the user's act

Dictation happens in the terminal UI: a key, `/voice-dictate`, or the palette's **Voice: dictate**. You cannot start a
microphone turn, and you must not pretend one happened. If the user asks how to dictate, tell them the key from
`voice_status` and that a pause sends the transcript, or opens a review dialog when `submit` is `review`.

## Not this plugin

- Transcribing an audio file: `utilities_speech_transcribe`.
- Meetings, calls or cloud realtime voice: not supported here.
- Reading a file aloud is `voice_speak` with the text, after the file is read with the file tools.

## Privacy

Never quote a transcript into a summary, a commit or a message unless the user asks. Audio and transcripts are local,
and the plugin keeps neither by default. A recording is a temp file deleted after the turn; do not look for it.

# Voice for OpenCode

Local voice dictation and read-aloud for OpenCode, powered by [Aurum](https://github.com/joe-broadhead/aurum): hold a key, speak, and the transcript is sent or reviewed, on device by default.

Unofficial; not affiliated with OpenCode or Anomaly.

## Requirements

- OpenCode `>=2.2.3 <2.3.0`, tested on 2.2.3, 2.2.4, 2.2.5 and 2.2.6.
- macOS on Apple silicon for the terminal UI; Linux (x64 or arm64) for engine mode (a host such as Jelly calls the plugin). The pinned Linux engine needs glibc 2.39 or newer (Ubuntu 24.04, Debian 13) and the ALSA runtime library (`libasound2`, or `libasound2t64` on Ubuntu 24.04). Status names what is missing.
- Aurum `0.0.24` or later. The engine is the pinned build in this plugin's GitHub release. `/voice-install` downloads it into the plugin cache, and it is verified against its SHA-256 before it runs. It is built from the [Aurum 0.0.24 release](https://github.com/joe-broadhead/aurum/releases/tag/v0.0.24). No `ffmpeg`, `afplay` or Rust toolchain is needed.

## Install

```bash
opencode plugin add github:joe-broadhead/opencode-voice#v0.0.1
```

Run `opencode reload`, or restart OpenCode, then run `/voice-status`.

Each release has its own tag, and a Git install does not update by itself. To move to a newer release, remove the old entry with `opencode plugin remove github:joe-broadhead/opencode-voice#v0.0.0`, then add the new tag with `opencode plugin add github:joe-broadhead/opencode-voice#v<version>`.

Or add the plugin to `opencode.json` instead, with the same spec:

```json
{ "plugins": [{ "package": "github:joe-broadhead/opencode-voice#v0.0.1" }] }
```

Run `/voice` and press `i`, or run `/voice-install`, to download the speech models and, when it is not already in the plugin cache, the pinned Aurum engine. The download asks first, names the size and hosts, and every file is verified against its pinned SHA-256 before the engine reads it. `/voice-install` from a script asks through the permission prompt; the dialog asks with a yes/no confirmation. The models are stored under the plugin cache (`~/Library/Caches/opencode-voice/engine` on macOS) and passed to Aurum as `--cache-dir`.

The engine downloads only through `/voice-install`. No tool call downloads it, and the speech tools register at setup, so restart OpenCode after `/voice-install`. `/voice-install` asks through the `voice_install` permission, which `access` sets: `all` allows it, `ask-changes` asks, and `read-only` denies it. To install under `read-only`, set `access` to `ask-changes` or `all`, run `/voice-install`, then set it back.

## Sign in

None. Voice is local: there is no account, no API key and no network call in the default path. A cloud speech provider is not part of this version.

## Use

- **Dictate:** press `ctrl+shift+space` (macOS) or `ctrl+space` (Linux), or run `/voice-dictate`. Speak, then pause; the transcript is sent to the active session. A second press ends the turn at once. `escape` cancels.
- **Review first:** set `"submit": "review"` to open a prefilled dialog instead of sending at once.
- **Read aloud:** run `/voice-speak` to hear the last reply, or set `"autoSpeak": true`.
- **Status:** run `/voice` or `/voice-status` for the engine, the models, the microphone and the one next step. `/voice-install` downloads missing models. In the dialog, `r` refreshes, `d` runs the doctor, `s` toggles send/review, `a` toggles auto-speak and `c` clears the opt-in history.
- **Engine mode:** a host such as hey-jelly calls `voice.dictation.engine` with audio and gets text; see [docs/engine.md](https://github.com/joe-broadhead/opencode-voice/blob/HEAD/docs/engine.md).

Audio stays on the machine. A recording is written to a private 0700 folder in the plugin cache, made mode 0600 when it closes, transcribed, and deleted on success, failure and cancel; transcripts are not kept unless `"keepTranscripts": true`, which stores the last 20 texts in OpenCode's plugin storage for Voice and is cleared with `c` in `/voice`.

## Permissions

**Every tool is allowed by default.** The plugin inserts this block after every agent's base `* * allow`. `access: "all"`
is the default, so this is the block in force:

<!-- rules:all -->
```json
[
  {"action": "voice_*", "resource": "*", "effect": "allow"},
  {"action": "voice_status", "resource": "*", "effect": "allow"},
  {"action": "voice_speak", "resource": "*", "effect": "allow"}
]
```
<!-- /rules:all -->

With `access: "ask-changes"`, status still runs and speaking asks:

<!-- rules:ask-changes -->
```json
[
  {"action": "voice_*", "resource": "*", "effect": "ask"},
  {"action": "voice_status", "resource": "*", "effect": "allow"},
  {"action": "voice_speak", "resource": "*", "effect": "ask"}
]
```
<!-- /rules:ask-changes -->

With `access: "read-only"`, status still runs and speaking is denied:

<!-- rules:read-only -->
```json
[
  {"action": "voice_*", "resource": "*", "effect": "deny"},
  {"action": "voice_status", "resource": "*", "effect": "allow"},
  {"action": "voice_speak", "resource": "*", "effect": "deny"}
]
```
<!-- /rules:read-only -->

So `voice_speak` reads text aloud on this machine whenever an agent decides to, with no prompt. That is sound on a
laptop whose speakers only you can hear; on a shared machine or a screen share, restrict it.

To restrict, choose one of three:

1. **`access`**, one option for the plugin: `"all"` (the default), `"ask-changes"` (status runs, speaking asks) or
   `"read-only"` (status runs, speaking is denied).
2. **An agent's own rules**, such as a silent agent:
   `"permissions": [{ "action": "voice_*", "resource": "*", "effect": "deny" }, { "action": "voice_status", "resource": "*", "effect": "allow" }]`.
3. **A per-tool rule** in your `opencode.json`: `{ "action": "voice_speak", "resource": "*", "effect": "ask" }`, or
   `"deny"` to turn speaking off.

An agent without a base allow gets no rules. `/voice` lists agents whose own rules would let a voice tool run without
asking, and prints the block for the access value in force.

## Configure

Options live in the plugin entry in `opencode.json`; every option and its error code is in [docs/configuration.md](https://github.com/joe-broadhead/opencode-voice/blob/HEAD/docs/configuration.md).

```json
{
  "plugins": [
    {
      "package": "github:joe-broadhead/opencode-voice#v0.0.1",
      "options": { "submit": "review", "autoSpeak": true, "voice": "Luna", "keybind": "ctrl+shift+space" }
    }
  ]
}
```

## Organisation rollout

A managed config can pre-set the options and point at a pre-seeded model folder:

```json
{
  "plugins": [
    {
      "package": "github:joe-broadhead/opencode-voice#v0.0.1",
      "options": { "assetsDir": "/opt/voice/models", "submit": "review" }
    }
  ]
}
```

The system config paths are `/etc/opencode/opencode.json` on Linux and `/Library/Application Support/opencode/opencode.json` on macOS. With `assetsDir`, the plugin never downloads; a missing or altered file is reported by `/voice`.

## Known limits

- Voice speaks through Aurum's local Kitten voice; a cloud provider is not part of this version.
- The microphone grant belongs to the terminal or host app that started OpenCode, not to the plugin. The `Access` row reports what the engine's doctor sees.
- A recording is at most 120 seconds. Aurum 0.0.24 accepts long audio; an older build without the `long_audio` capability accepts 30 seconds per utterance and the plugin says so.
- Voice has no speech engine for Intel Macs (x64) or Windows: no pinned Aurum package is published for them. On those systems
  the plugin loads, status reports `UNSUPPORTED_PLATFORM`, and installing refuses before any download. A local Aurum binary
  you point at with `aurumPath` or `VOICE_AURUM_PATH` does run there.
- Linux systems with glibc older than 2.39 (Ubuntu 22.04, Debian 12) cannot run the pinned engine. Status names the
  symbol version it needs and the systems that have it.
- The speech engine downloads only through `/voice-install`, which asks through the `voice_install` permission. `read-only` denies that permission, so install with `access` set to `ask-changes` or `all`. No tool call downloads the engine, and the speech tools register at setup, so restart OpenCode after `/voice-install`. That `read-only` denial rests on the permission rule and a unit test (`test/unit/config.test.ts`); it is not verified through the host's command route.
- **Jelly.** The settings declare their choices and bounds, which only a Jelly that includes app#1301 reads; an older Jelly refuses the plugin's declaration.
- Updates are not automatic for a Git install, and `opencode plugin update` and `opencode plugin check` do not work on one: to move to a newer release, remove the old entry and add the new tag.

## Troubleshooting

| Code | What to do |
|---|---|
| `ENGINE_MISSING` | Run `/voice-install` to download the pinned speech engine, then run `/voice-status`. |
| `ENGINE_UNVERIFIED` | Run `/voice-install` to replace the engine; a binary whose digest does not match is never run. |
| `ENGINE_INCOMPATIBLE` | Install Aurum 0.0.24 or later. |
| `ENGINE_EXITED` | Run the doctor in `/voice`, then try again. |
| `UNSUPPORTED_PLATFORM` | Use macOS on Apple silicon or Linux, or set `aurumPath` to a local engine. |
| `UNSUPPORTED` | Use a supported platform and engine. |
| `MODEL_MISSING` | Run `/voice-install` and approve the download. |
| `MODEL_DOWNLOAD_FAILED` | Retry `/voice-install`; if it persists, check the network or proxy. |
| `INTEGRITY_MISMATCH` | Retry `/voice-install`; a model that does not match its hash is never used. |
| `MIC_DENIED` | Grant microphone access in System Settings → Privacy & Security → Microphone. |
| `MIC_UNAVAILABLE` | Connect a microphone, then run `/voice-dictate` again. |
| `AUDIO_DEVICE_MISSING` | Connect an output device, then try again. |
| `NO_SPEECH` | Speak again, a little closer to the microphone. |
| `AUDIO_TOO_LONG` | Shorten the recording or the text. |
| `INPUT_INVALID` | Fix the call's input as the message says, then call it again. |
| `UNCHECKED` | Call it from a session, where its approval can be answered. |
| `BAD_AUDIO` | Send a WAV file, 16 kHz, mono, 16-bit PCM. |
| `BUSY` | Wait for the current dictation, or press `escape`. |
| `TIMEOUT` | Try again, then run the doctor in `/voice`. |
| `CANCELLED` | Nothing to do. |
| `SIDECAR_FAILED` | Run the doctor in `/voice`, then try again. |
| `PROVIDER_AUTH_REQUIRED` | Add the provider key, or choose a local model in `/voice`. |
| `PROVIDER_FAILED` | Try again, or choose a local model in `/voice`. |
| `HOST_UNTESTED` | Use OpenCode `>=2.2.3 <2.3.0`, or set `allowUntestedHost`. |
| `OPTIONS_INVALID` | Fix the named option in `opencode.json`. |
| `STATUS_UNAVAILABLE` | Try again, then run the doctor in `/voice`. |
| `SKILLS_INVALID` | Reinstall the plugin from `github:joe-broadhead/opencode-voice#v0.0.1`. |

## Uninstall

```bash
opencode plugin remove github:joe-broadhead/opencode-voice#v0.0.1
```

The model cache stays under the platform cache folder (`~/Library/Caches/opencode-voice` on macOS, `~/.cache/opencode-voice` on Linux); delete it to remove the models too.

# Controls

- **no-skill:** the same prompt with the `voice` skill renamed away. If it passes, the skill adds nothing for that case.
- **old-version 0.0.0:** the previous release's skill and tool descriptions, copied by the runner's `--skill-file`.
- **expect-fail:** `speak-asks` has a refusal arm (`speak-refused-none`) that must stay failing when the approval is
  removed. A green refusal arm means the permission test is not measuring what it claims.

# Changelog

All notable changes to this project are documented here. The format is based on
[Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/), and this project adheres to
[Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/spec/v2.0.0.html).

## [0.0.1] - 2026-11-13

### Added

- The `jelly` settings declare their choices: `access` offers Jelly's three choices, **Allowed**, **Ask before
  changes** and **Read only**, and `maxRecordSeconds` is declared as a whole number from 5 to 120, the options
  parser's own set and bounds (needs a jelly that includes app#1301). `submit` and `statusIndicator` are not declared:
  they apply only to OpenCode's terminal UI and do nothing in Jelly; they stay options in `opencode.json`.

## [0.0.0] - 2026-11-10
<!-- kit-release: the GitHub release v0.0.0 -->

### Added

- Push-to-talk and hands-free dictation in the terminal UI, sending on pause or opening a prefilled review dialog,
  with `escape` to cancel.
- Read the last reply aloud, and opt-in auto-speak, with the local Kitten voice.
- One status dialog and `/voice-status`, covering the engine, the models, the microphone, the tools, the agents without
  default rules and one next step.
- `/voice-install`, which downloads the pinned models, verifies their size and SHA-256, and reports each file.
- `voice_status` and `voice_speak` agent tools, and the `voice.dictation.tools` RPC with `describe`.
- The `voice.dictation.engine` RPC for hosts such as hey-jelly: status, warmup, transcribe, synthesize and cancel.
- The pinned Aurum 0.0.24 engine for macOS on Apple silicon and for Linux x64 and arm64 (glibc), downloaded by
  `/voice-install` from this plugin's GitHub release, verified by SHA-256 before it runs, with no `ffmpeg`, `afplay` or
  Rust toolchain.
- The `voice` skill, the `jelly` declaration and the family icon.
- A Jelly `access` setting, with `all`, `ask-changes` and `read-only`, as the other plugins declare it.

### Changed

- Every tool is allowed by default: the plugin inserts one `allow` rule for the `voice_*` pattern and one for each of
  `voice_status` and `voice_speak` after every agent's base rule, so speaking a reply aloud runs with no prompt and a
  tool Voice adds later runs at once. An agent's own rules, your `permissions` and a saved approval still win.
- The `access` option restricts that in one line: `"all"` (the default), `"ask-changes"` (status runs, speaking asks)
  and `"read-only"` (status runs, speaking is denied). The README prints the block for each value, and `/voice-status`
  shows the one in force.
- A missing engine says to run `/voice-install`, which downloads the pinned engine into the plugin cache; a reinstall is
  not needed.
- Windows reports `UNSUPPORTED_PLATFORM`, not a missing install, and the next step names Linux as well as macOS.
- An Aurum binary set with `aurumPath` or `VOICE_AURUM_PATH` runs on Intel Macs, which have no pinned engine; status no
  longer calls it unsupported, and no longer tells you to reinstall a binary you chose.
- On Linux, an engine that cannot load its ALSA runtime library, or that needs a newer C library than the system has, is
  reported by name with the next step, instead of as an incompatible engine.

# Contributing

## Setup

Requires Node 24 and Bun 1.4.4 (the Bun inside stock OpenCode 2.2.3–2.2.6).

```bash
npm ci --ignore-scripts
npm run stock:install                 # the four tested stock releases, into .cache/stock
node scripts/build-native.mjs --ensure # the pinned engine for this computer, into .cache/bin, verified
npm run check
```

`npm run check` runs every stage: typecheck, unit tests, the build, the icons, the copy checks, the forbidden scan, the
eval pack's static tier, the host suite on each stock release and the pack test. Run one stage with
`node scripts/check.mjs <stage>`.

## Host tests

The host suite starts a real stock OpenCode server for each tested release. `npm run stock:install` installs the four
releases into `.cache/stock`. To use other binaries, set `OPENCODE_BIN_<version>` for one release, for example
`OPENCODE_BIN_2_2_5=/path/to/opencode npm run check`. With neither, the host stage is skipped and says so; in CI a gap
fails the build. The host tests use the same gate (`test/support/stock-gate.ts`): a missing release skips with a notice
on a laptop and fails in CI. The CI workflow installs the four releases and exports `OPENCODE_BIN_<version>`. The tests use
an isolated `HOME`, `XDG_*` and
`TMPDIR`, a loopback server, a dead proxy, and the fake engine in `test/fixtures`; they never touch a real OpenCode, a
microphone or a provider.

## The engine

A real engine run on Linux needs glibc 2.39 or newer and the ALSA runtime (`libasound2`,
or `libasound2t64` on Ubuntu 24.04). The CI runners are Ubuntu 24.04 and have both.
Development and tests use `test/fixtures/fake-aurum.mjs` through `VOICE_AURUM_PATH`. It answers the sidecar protocol, the
recorder, the player and the doctor. A real engine can be used with `aurumPath` or `VOICE_AURUM_PATH`. The release
files come from `node scripts/build-native.mjs --release <dir>`, which the `native` workflow runs: it downloads each pinned
binary named in `manifest/aurum.json`, checks its size and SHA-256, and gzips it. `.cache/` is git-ignored and never committed.

## Rules

- Every bundle stays self-contained: no relative imports in `dist/`, and only the host's modules external.
- The shared tools RPC (`src/host/tools-rpc.ts`) is copied from the family's shared source; edit only its
  PLUGIN-SPECIFIC block, and run `node scripts/check-copies.mjs`.
- The icon contract is enforced by `scripts/check-icons.mjs`; regenerate both PNGs from `assets/icon.svg`.
- Never add a provider call, a telemetry call or a network request to status, dictation or read-aloud.
- Every error code has a row in the README and `docs/configuration.md`; a test fails otherwise.

## Releasing

Each release is the GitHub tag `v<version>`, where `<version>` is the `version` in `package.json`, and users install from
that tag. The release is one commit on top of a `master` head that CI passed, and the tag points at it. The release
workflow makes both, in GitHub Actions: nobody builds, commits or tags a release on their own machine, and no personal
key signs it.

While changes land, their notes go under `## [Unreleased]` at the top of `CHANGELOG.md`. Each earlier GitHub release is
a `## [x.y.z] - YYYY-MM-DD` heading below it, newest first, and the npm history stays last, under
`## Earlier releases on npm`.

1. On `master`, set `version` in `package.json` to the new version, and change every install spec in the README,
   `CONTRIBUTING.md` and `docs/` to `#v<version>` (`test/docs.test.ts` fails until they match). Then run
   `node scripts/changelog.mjs release`: it turns `## [Unreleased]` into `## [<version>] - <today>`, above the earlier
   releases, and refuses a CHANGELOG it cannot shape. Run `npm run check`.
2. Push that commit to `master`, and wait for CI to pass on it.
3. Run the `native` workflow on that commit (`gh workflow run native.yml --ref master`), and wait for it to pass. It
   builds the release files for `v<version>`.
4. Start the release with that commit's full sha and the native run's id:
   `gh workflow run release.yml --ref master -f sha=<full sha> -f native_run=<native run id>`, or from Actions → release →
   Run workflow, on `master`.
5. Read the run's summary, then approve the `release` environment. The summary is on the run page, under the `stage`
   job: the tag, the parent and its CI run, the release commit and its tree, the sha256 of `SHA256SUMS` and the staged
   artifact's id, `SHA256SUMS` itself, and the notes. Open the release commit on `release/v<version>` and read them
   before approving: the approval releases exactly those bytes. Only the owner approves a release. Agents never approve
   one, never call the deployment-approval API, and never bypass a ruleset or the environment; the kit's scripts make
   only their own GitHub calls and refuse every other.
6. Check the published Release: not a draft, its notes, and every asset against `SHA256SUMS`.

Before the approval, the workflow:
- **plans:** refuses a run that is not on `master`, a sha that is not `master`'s head, a sha without a successful `ci.yml`
  push run, a version that is not `x.y.z`, a CHANGELOG whose newest release is not this version, a release that does not
  move forward from the last published Release, a leftover `release/v<version>` branch, a native run that did not build
  this sha on `master`, by hand, with success, and a missing `native_run` (or one given to a plugin that is not native);
- **builds** `dist/` with `npm ci --ignore-scripts` and `npm run build`, with a read-only token, and writes the release
  files: `dist/`, `package.json` without its lifecycle scripts, and the vetted native manifest;
- **commits** them on a temporary branch `release/v<version>` at the parent, through GitHub's API with the workflow's token,
  so GitHub signs the commit (author `github-actions[bot]`, committer GitHub). This job runs no npm. It refuses a commit
  that GitHub does not verify, or whose parent or tree is not the one the files give;
- **verifies** on a fresh runner: the commit's identity, one parent on `master`, `package.json` exactly the parent's
  without the lifecycle scripts, only regular files in the allowed paths, no `package.json` under `dist/`, and a second,
  independent build of the parent (its own job) equal to the committed `dist/` byte for byte;
- **installs** the release commit with `plugin add` on each stock OpenCode host (2.2.3 to 2.2.6);
- **packs** the commit before installing anything and keeps that tarball, then runs the pack stage against a copy;
- **stages** the Release: verifies the attested native files, writes `SHA256SUMS` and the notes (the version's CHANGELOG
  section), and shows them all in the run summary with the sha256 of `SHA256SUMS`.

A job either runs repository or dependency code (`npm ci`, the build, the pack stage, a host install) and has no write
token, or uses the API and runs only the kit's scripts on a fresh checkout, after checking that the release commit's
`scripts/` and `.github/` are the parent's. The first kind is not token-free: `actions/checkout` fetches with the job's
read-only (`contents: read`) token, and its post step and the artifact uploads run after repository code on the same
runner, so that code could reach a read-only token for this public repository and the runner's artifact token. Jobs
pass files as artifacts downloaded by the id the uploading job gave, and each is checked again on arrival.

After the approval, it downloads the staged artifact by the id the summary names, and refuses unless `SHA256SUMS` has
the sha256 the summary shows and every staged file matches it, and every native file is the one the release commit's
`manifest/native.json` pins, size and sha256, with each gzip holding the pinned executable. Then it checks everything again, creates the annotated tag
`v<version>` on the release commit (tagger `github-actions[bot]`, unsigned), checks the tag, creates the Release with the
notes, the tarball, the native files and `SHA256SUMS`, and deletes `release/v<version>`. The tag keeps the commit.

GitHub's signature and the bot identity show only that GitHub made the commit through its API for the workflow; anyone
with write access can make such a commit. What ties the release to `master` is its content: one parent CI passed, the
exact `package.json`, the allowed paths and the byte-for-byte rebuild. Never relax those because the commit is signed.

**A rejected, expired or failed run** leaves nothing behind: the `cleanup` job deletes `release/v<version>` when it points
at the parent or at that run's commit, and never touches another branch. No tag exists before the approval, so the
version is not burned: fix `master` and start again. If `cleanup` itself failed, the next run refuses until the branch
is deleted: `gh api -X DELETE repos/joe-broadhead/opencode-voice/git/refs/heads/release/v<version>`.

**Resume.** If the run fails after creating the tag and before the Release is complete, start it again with the same `sha`
and `native_run`. The plan finds the kit's tag on a release commit on that sha with no published Release, and resumes:
it makes no new commit, checks and installs the tagged commit, stages the files, and after a new approval reuses the tag
and adds what the Release lacks. Delete a draft Release a failed upload left first: the publish step refuses a draft.
Any other existing tag is refused: release the next version.

The repository's tag ruleset keeps a `v*` tag from being moved or deleted. A stray `v*` tag, one that never became a
Release, does not block later releases: only published Releases count, and drafts do not. Its version cannot be
released, so release the next one. To remove the tag anyway, an admin disables the `release tags` ruleset, deletes the
tag, and restores the ruleset exactly as it was.

**Known limit: a `v*` tag pushed by hand.** No ruleset limits who creates a `v*` tag, so anyone with write access can
push one by hand, pointing at any commit. Such a tag has no published Release, the forward-only check ignores it, and
Jelly installs only a published Release whose `SHA256SUMS` it verifies. But a user who installs
`github:joe-broadhead/opencode-voice#v<x>` directly gets whatever that tag points at. Only the release workflow makes
release tags; never push one by hand.

The release kit is these files, the same in every plugin: `scripts/release-rules.mjs`, `scripts/release-commit.mjs`,
`scripts/release-github.mjs`, `scripts/check-release-shape.mjs`, `scripts/changelog.mjs`, `scripts/release-version.mjs`,
`scripts/release-pack.mjs`, `scripts/publish-release.mjs`, `scripts/attach-native.mjs`, `scripts/native-manifest.mjs`,
`scripts/tested-hosts.mjs`, `scripts/check-release-plugin-add.sh`, `scripts/release-kit.test.mjs` and
`.github/workflows/release.yml`. Do not re-run the older `apply-release-kit.mjs`: it writes back the kit that could
release only `v0.0.0`.

Each release has its own tag, and a Git install does not update by itself. To move to a newer release, remove the old entry with `opencode plugin remove github:joe-broadhead/opencode-voice#v<old version>`, then add the new tag with `opencode plugin add github:joe-broadhead/opencode-voice#v<version>`.

Or add the plugin to `opencode.json` instead, with the same spec:

```json
{ "plugins": [{ "package": "github:joe-broadhead/opencode-voice#v0.0.1" }] }
```

# Security

## Supported versions

Only the latest release is supported. Voice is tested on 2.2.3, 2.2.4, 2.2.5 and 2.2.6.

## Reporting a vulnerability

Report it through GitHub's private vulnerability reporting on
[github.com/joe-broadhead/opencode-voice](https://github.com/joe-broadhead/opencode-voice/security/advisories/new).
Do not open a public issue.

## Data handling

- **Audio never leaves the machine.** The speech providers are local. No cloud provider is part of this version.
- **Recordings are not kept.** A turn is a temp WAV in the plugin's cache, mode 0600, deleted after transcription, on
  error, on cancel and on dispose. There is no audio history.
- **Transcript text is not kept by default.** With `keepTranscripts`, the last 20 transcripts are stored as text in
  OpenCode's plugin storage for Voice and can be cleared with `c` in `/voice`.
- **No secrets in output.** Status, errors, commands and logs carry no transcript, no audio, no key and no absolute path
  outside the plugin's cache. `src/redact.ts` is applied to host and engine text.
- **Models are verified.** Every downloaded file is checked against an exact size and SHA-256 before it is renamed into
  the engine cache. Each role's files are verified again before the engine first reads them, and `/voice-install`
  verifies every file it wrote; a mismatch is `INTEGRITY_MISMATCH` and the file is never used.
- **The engine is pinned.** Each release file holds a binary whose size and digest are checked against the release manifest before
  it runs; a mismatch is `ENGINE_UNVERIFIED` and nothing starts. The engine must report Aurum 0.0.24 or later and its
  sidecar must advertise `transcribe`, or the plugin refuses with `ENGINE_INCOMPATIBLE`. `aurumPath` is a developer and
  organisation seam; `VOICE_AURUM_PATH` is the test seam. A binary found only on `PATH` is never run. The engine `/voice-install` downloads is checked against the SHA-256 in the pinned release manifest before it is made executable or started.
- **The install asks.** `/voice-install` asserts `voice_install` with the asset names, hosts and total size before the
  first request; the dialog asks with a yes/no confirmation. Installers serialise on a lock file, and a download
  follows redirects only to the pinned host over HTTPS.
- **Text is redacted.** Engine and host text that reaches status, the dialog, an error or the RPC is reduced to one line
  with token shapes removed; a status failure never echoes a path.
- **The microphone is never bypassed.** The OS grant belongs to the responsible process; the plugin reports it and links
  to System Settings.

## Permissions

**Every tool is allowed by default.** The plugin inserts a block after each agent's base allow that allows both tools,
so an agent can make the machine speak — out loud, on your speakers or a screen share — with no prompt. The `access`
option restricts that in one line (`"ask-changes"` asks each time, `"read-only"` denies speaking), and a per-tool rule
does it for `voice_speak` alone. The paste-ready block for an agent that must not ask is in `docs/configuration.md`.

`voice_speak` asserts its own permission inside its `execute`, because OpenCode does not enforce a plugin tool's declared
`ask`. From a script, an `ask` is refused with `PERMISSION_DENIED`, with no prompt and no tool call.

Voice writes audio, recordings and models only under its own cache (`~/Library/Caches/opencode-voice` on macOS, the
equivalent elsewhere): no tool, command or RPC takes a file path from you or from an agent, so no `external_directory`
rule is involved on either side.

## Scripts

The tools RPC (`voice.dictation.tools`) runs only `allow` rules, refuses an `ask` before dispatch, and never runs a
`deny`. The shared module is pinned by `scripts/check-copies.mjs`; do not edit its shared part in this repository.

# Architecture

Voice has the family's two entries and a host-agnostic engine core:

```
src/index.ts       server part: tools, tools RPC, status RPC, engine RPC, commands, rules
src/tui.tsx        terminal UI part: one dialog, the keymap, dictation and read-aloud
src/engine/        Aurum: the sidecar, the recorder, the player, WAV, models, the doctor
src/dictation/     the state machine and the one dictation flow
src/status.ts      the one status model
src/host/          the shared tools RPC, the default rules, the tools
```

Each entry is bundled into one self-contained file, `dist/index.js` and `dist/tui.js`, with shared code inlined and only
the host's modules external. The tools RPC contract is plain JSON Schema; `dist/tui.js` carries no zod.

## Processes

```
OpenCode TUI process
  plugin TUI part
    ├─ aurum record -O <wav> --level-events   (one child per utterance)
    ├─ aurum play <wav>                       (one child per reply)
    └─ sidecar client ── JSONL ──▶ aurum converse --stdio (warm)
                                      ├─ whisper.cpp STT
                                      └─ Kitten TTS

OpenCode server process
  plugin server part
    ├─ voice.dictation.tools   (voice_status, voice_speak)
    ├─ voice.dictation.status  (the status model)
    └─ voice.dictation.engine  (a host such as Jelly)
```

The two parts are separate processes and do not share a sidecar or a temp folder. Each starts its own only when used,
and each removes only its own temp folder on dispose. Under a host such as Jelly only the server part loads, so there is
one.

## Platform facts

- OpenCode 2.2.3, 2.2.4, 2.2.5 and 2.2.6 have **no composer API in the terminal UI**. A transcript reaches the prompt either by
  `client.session.prompt` (send) or by a prefilled `ui.dialog.prompt` (review). The desktop GUI entry does have
  `screen.composer.insert`, which is a later surface.
- A TUI plugin registers a key with `keymap.layer`; `keymap.shortcuts` reports the binding. The OS may still take a
  combination before the plugin sees it; macOS uses `ctrl+space` for input-source switching, which is why the default
  there is `ctrl+shift+space`.
- The microphone grant belongs to the responsible process (the terminal or the host app). A child of OpenCode inherits
  that decision; the plugin reports it and never bypasses it.
- The engine is not run in the host's process: it is a pinned binary, verified by digest, and every child is killed by
  the PID the plugin recorded.

## The engine

`aurum converse --stdio` is a long-lived JSONL process. Commands: `transcribe {path}`, `synthesize {text, path}`,
`abort`, `shutdown`. Events: `ready` with `caps`, `user_final`, `synthesized`, `error`, `shutdown`. The plugin keeps one
request in flight, queues the rest, restarts once after a crash, and never lets a late event resolve a timed-out request.

`aurum record` owns the microphone so the plugin needs no `ffmpeg`; `aurum play` owns the speaker so it needs no
`afplay`. Both are part of Aurum 0.0.24, the release this plugin requires. `/voice-install` downloads the pinned binary from this plugin's GitHub release into `<cache>/native/v0.0.0/aurum/<platform>/aurum`, verifies its size and SHA-256 and makes it executable; an `aurumPath` option or `VOICE_AURUM_PATH` takes precedence. A one-shot `aurum transcribe` fallback is not
used. The engine's `--version` is checked before the sidecar starts; a binary older than 0.0.24 is refused.

Silence never reaches the model: the plugin measures the WAV (peak and voiced milliseconds) and returns `NO_SPEECH`.

## The models

Models are downloaded, never shipped. The manifest (`manifest/models.json`) is built from Aurum's reviewed catalogue and
pinned by exact size, SHA-256 and revision. Files live under `<platform cache>/opencode-voice/engine/{models,tts}`, the
layout Aurum expects, and that folder is passed to every engine command as `--cache-dir`, so the file `/voice-install`
writes is the file the sidecar reads. Each role's files are hashed again before the engine first reads them. `assetsDir`
takes precedence for a pre-seeded install and forbids downloading.

## Verified with Aurum 0.0.24

On macOS arm64 (2026-11-07), against the released `aurum-macos-arm64` (SHA-256 `a8d72bbe…3cce764`), in an isolated cache:
the engine install downloaded 48,211,872 bytes in 3.6 s cold and verified; a one-byte alteration was refused
`ENGINE_UNVERIFIED`; `models prepare tiny-q5_1` took 39.3 s cold (36.3 s load) and 1.8 s warm; the sidecar reported
`ready.caps` `transcribe, synthesize, synthesize_speaking_rate, synthesize_abort, long_audio` and became ready in
0.53 s; the three `say -o` fixtures transcribed in 0.18–0.52 s with exact text, and a warm repeat took 0.19 s.
Synthesis wrote a 24 kHz WAV, and `aurum play` played a silent file without a device change.

## Errors and status

One status model drives the dialog, `/voice-status`, the status RPC and `voice_status`. Its shared fields are `version`,
`host`, `state`, `unguardedAgents` and `nextStep`; the rest are Voice's. Errors use the family shape, and each code has a
row in `docs/configuration.md` and the README, enforced by a test.

# Configuration

Every option is read from the plugin entry in `opencode.json`. An unknown option is refused with `OPTIONS_INVALID` and
the field's name; no option value is ever echoed in an error, a log or status.

| Option | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `submit` | `"send"` \| `"review"` | `"send"` | Send the transcript at once, or open a prefilled dialog first. |
| `keybind` | string | `ctrl+shift+space` on macOS, `ctrl+space` on Linux | The dictation key, in OpenCode's keymap syntax. |
| `autoSpeak` | boolean | `false` | Read every completed reply aloud. |
| `voice` | string | `"Luna"` | The local TTS voice, passed to the engine as `--voice`. |
| `sttModel` | string | `"tiny-q5_1"` | The local STT model, as Aurum names it. |
| `language` | string | `"auto"` | A spoken language code, or `auto`. |
| `maxRecordSeconds` | integer 5–120 | `120` | The longest recording. |
| `statusIndicator` | `"toast"` \| `"footer"` | `"toast"` | A toast, or an opt-in row above the prompt while listening. |
| `keepTranscripts` | boolean | `false` | Keep the last 20 transcripts as text, in OpenCode's plugin storage for Voice, cleared with `c` in `/voice`. Audio is never kept. |
| `allowUntestedHost` | boolean | `false` | Run on an OpenCode version outside the supported range. |
| `engine` | boolean | `true` | Register the `voice.dictation.engine` RPC a host such as Jelly calls. |
| `access` | `"all"` \| `"ask-changes"` \| `"read-only"` | `"all"` | What the plugin's own tools may do without asking. A user's later rule still wins. |
| `aurumPath` | string | — | A developer or organisation engine binary. It is labelled unverified unless it matches the pinned digest. |
| `assetsDir` | string | — | A pre-seeded model folder. Nothing is downloaded. |

## Permissions

**Every tool is allowed by default.** The plugin adds this block to every agent that has a base `* * allow`, after it
and before the agent's own rules:

```
{ "action": "voice_*", "resource": "*", "effect": "allow" },
{ "action": "voice_status", "resource": "*", "effect": "allow" },
{ "action": "voice_speak", "resource": "*", "effect": "allow" }
```

`voice_speak` reads text aloud on this machine whenever an agent decides to, with no prompt. `access` restricts it:
`"ask-changes"` asks for speaking, and `"read-only"` denies it; the reads always run. A later rule of the user's wins,
and a rule for one tool does it for that tool (`{ "action": "voice_speak", "resource": "*", "effect": "deny" }`).

Agents without a base allow get no rules. An agent is listed as without default rules when it has a base allow, lacks
the block, and its own rules would run an unnamed `voice_*` tool without asking.

The paste-ready block for an agent that must never ask:

```json
{
  "agents": {
    "build": {
      "permissions": [
        { "action": "*", "resource": "*", "effect": "deny" },
        { "action": "read", "resource": "*", "effect": "allow" },
        { "action": "glob", "resource": "*", "effect": "allow" },
        { "action": "grep", "resource": "*", "effect": "allow" },
        { "action": "list", "resource": "*", "effect": "allow" },
        { "action": "voice_status", "resource": "*", "effect": "allow" }
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

## The engine

The engine downloads only through `/voice-install`. No tool call downloads it. `/voice-install` asks through the `voice_install` permission, which `access` sets: `all` allows it, `ask-changes` asks, and `read-only` denies it, so install with `access` set to `ask-changes` or `all`. The speech tools register at setup, so restart OpenCode after the install.

## Errors

Every error is `CODE: what happened. Next step: What to do.` The codes are:

| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `ENGINE_MISSING` | The pinned Aurum engine is not in the plugin cache. Run `/voice-install`. |
| `ENGINE_UNVERIFIED` | The cached engine's size or SHA-256 does not match the release manifest; nothing starts. Run `/voice-install` to replace it. |
| `ENGINE_INCOMPATIBLE` | The binary is older than 0.0.24 or lacks a required capability. |
| `ENGINE_EXITED` | The sidecar process exited. |
| `UNSUPPORTED_PLATFORM` | No engine build exists for this OS and architecture. |
| `UNSUPPORTED` | The platform or engine cannot run. |
| `MODEL_MISSING` | A model is not cached, or a pre-seeded folder lacks it. Run `/voice-install` and approve the download. |
| `MODEL_DOWNLOAD_FAILED` | A download failed, stalled, or had the wrong size. |
| `INTEGRITY_MISMATCH` | A model does not match its pinned SHA-256, before or after a download; it is never used. |
| `MIC_DENIED` | The OS refused microphone access. |
| `MIC_UNAVAILABLE` | No input device is available; connect a microphone and run `/voice-dictate` again. |
| `AUDIO_DEVICE_MISSING` | No output device is available; connect one and try again. |
| `NO_SPEECH` | The recording held no speech, or under 160 ms of voiced audio. |
| `AUDIO_TOO_LONG` | Audio or text exceeded the wire limit. |
| `BAD_AUDIO` | Not a WAV, or not 16 kHz mono 16-bit PCM. |
| `UNCHECKED` | A tool that changes something was called with nothing to check its permission against. |
| `INPUT_INVALID` | The call's own input is wrong, such as empty text or more than 5,000 characters. |
| `BUSY` | A dictation, synthesis or playback is already running. |
| `TIMEOUT` | The engine did not answer in time. |
| `CANCELLED` | The user cancelled. |
| `SIDECAR_FAILED` | The engine failed or could not start. |
| `PROVIDER_AUTH_REQUIRED` | A cloud provider has no key. |
| `PROVIDER_FAILED` | A cloud provider returned an error. |
| `HOST_UNTESTED` | OpenCode is outside `>=2.2.3 <2.3.0`. |
| `OPTIONS_INVALID` | An option is malformed or unknown. |
| `STATUS_UNAVAILABLE` | The status model could not be read. |
| `SKILLS_INVALID` | A skill file is malformed. |

## Privacy

- Audio never leaves the machine: the default providers are local, and no cloud provider is part of this version.
- A recording is a temp WAV in a private 0700 folder in the plugin's cache, made mode 0600 when it closes, and deleted
  after transcription, on error, on cancel and on dispose. There is no audio history.
- Transcript text is kept only with `keepTranscripts`, as the last 20 entries in OpenCode's plugin storage for Voice,
  with a clear-all action (`c` in `/voice`).
- No transcript, audio, key or absolute path outside the plugin's cache appears in status, errors or logs.
- The microphone grant belongs to the process that started OpenCode (the terminal or the host app), not to the plugin.
  The status row reports what the engine's doctor sees and links to the OS setting; the plugin never bypasses it.

# Engine contract: `voice.dictation.engine`

A host that runs OpenCode headless, such as [hey-jelly](https://github.com/joe-broadhead/hey-jelly), captures audio,
endpoints the turn and calls this RPC. The plugin owns the engine, the models, the silence check and the temp files; the
host owns the microphone, the submit mode, the conversation loop and playback.

This contract is shared word for word with `hey-jelly/VOICE.md`. Change it in both places, or bump `v`.

## Transport

- Register the RPC in the OpenCode server with `ctx.rpc.register({ id: "voice.dictation.engine", ... })`.
- Call it with `client.rpc({ id: "voice.dictation.engine", methods })[name](input, { location })`.
- Every input and output carries `v: 1`. The RPC schema refuses an unknown `v` with the host's validation error.
- Audio crosses as base64 inside JSON, never as device access. The plugin never opens a microphone or a speaker here.
- The HTTP envelope is `{"input": { ...the method input... }}`.

## Methods

| Method | Input | Output |
|---|---|---|
| `status` | `{ v }` | `{ v, ready, stt: { provider, model, language }, tts: { provider, model, voice }, models, caps, problems }` |
| `warmup` | `{ v }` | `{ v, ready, state }` — starts the sidecar and loads the model |
| `transcribe` | `{ v, audio, mime: "audio/wav", language? }` | `{ v, text, silent, ms, provider, model }` |
| `synthesize` | `{ v, text, markdown?, rate? }` | `{ v, audio, mime: "audio/wav", spokenText, truncated }` |
| `cancel` | `{ v }` | `{ v }` |

- Input audio is WAV, 16 kHz, mono, 16-bit PCM, at most 120 s. Anything else is `BAD_AUDIO`. A build without the
  `long_audio` capability accepts 30 s per utterance; `AUDIO_TOO_LONG` names it.
- `silent` is the speech gate: no sound, or under 160 ms of voiced audio. No transcription is attempted, and `text` is
  `""`.
- `caps` contains `transcribe`, `synthesize`, `warmup` and `cancel`, and `synthesize_speaking_rate` when the build can
  apply `rate`. The engine's caps are complete after `warmup`; a host that needs them calls it first. A `rate` other
  than 1 without that cap is refused with `UNSUPPORTED`.
- `engine.cancel` aborts the in-flight request and any queued request issued before it. A cancelled call rejects as
  `CANCELLED`. Requests are serialised: a host may overlap two calls, and each settles with its own payload.
- Streaming partial transcripts are not part of v1. A later `v: 2` adds them; the request and response methods stay.

## Errors

A failed call rejects with `{ type: "failed", message, data: { code, next } }`. `message` is the full
`CODE: what happened. Next step: What to do.`; `next` is the next step alone. Codes are the plugin's own
(`docs/configuration.md`), and the messages never carry audio, a transcript or a key.

## Ownership

| Concern | Owner |
|---|---|
| Microphone capture, device choice, permission prompts | The host |
| End of turn, live level, no-speech timeout | The host |
| Submit mode, conversation loop, playback | The host |
| The sidecar lifecycle, queueing, timeouts, restart | The plugin |
| STT/TTS providers, models, voices | The plugin |
| Silence check, speakable reduction, temp files, doctor | The plugin |

# In Jelly

[Jelly](https://heyjelly.ai) runs OpenCode agents. It reads the `jelly` section of this package's `package.json` as JSON,
without loading the plugin, when a person reviews the exact version.

Jelly names the plugin **Voice** (`jelly.title`), with the package name and version beneath. Under that name it shows the
one line in `jelly.summary`, and beside it the mark in `jelly.icon` (`assets/icon.svg`, shipped in the package): Jelly
reads that file once, when it records the plugin, and keeps it only if it is a clean SVG of drawing elements, with no
script, style, link or outside reference. The mark is the family's Neutral slate tile — a prompt caret and three sound
bars, drawn by us — and not any vendor's logo or letterform.

## Icons and vendor

`jelly.icon` stays `assets/icon.svg`, and `opencode.icons` declares the same mark three ways, in MCP's `Icon` shape: the
clean SVG (`sizes: ["any"]`), a 128×128 PNG and a 256×256 PNG, each with its `mimeType` and a relative `src` inside the
package. `opencode.icons[0].src` equals `jelly.icon`, so the two declarations cannot drift. `exports` exposes the three
files as `./icon.svg`, `./icon-128.png` and `./icon-256.png`, and all three ship in the tarball.

`opencode.vendor` is absent: Voice is our own product. The engine is Aurum, which is ours too, and no vendor mark,
colour or letterform is shipped.

## Tools and permissions

2 tools are declared (1 read-only): `voice_status` and `voice_speak` both run. Jelly's agents have no base "allow
everything" rule, so this plugin's own default rules, which it puts after that rule, never reach them. Jelly writes each
declared effect as that tool's default instead (the person's own choice replaces it).

- `voice_status` (`allow`, read-only): the engine, models, microphone and next step.
- `voice_speak` (`allow`): speaks text on the machine. It is an action, not a read, so `access: "ask-changes"` or a
  rule of the person's can make it ask.

A tool Voice adds later is not declared, so in Jelly it is not asked about until a new version declares it. Keep
`jelly.tools` in step with `src/host/tools.ts`; `test/unit/jelly.test.ts` checks the list and each effect against the
plugin's own default rules.

## Skills

Declared: `voice`. Jelly refuses an install whose skill ids collide with another plugin's or the agent's own; `voice` is
distinct from `utilities-speech`, `slack-search` and the neighbours' meeting skills.

## Views and RPC

No views, feeds, widgets, sign-ins or work kinds. The `voice.dictation.engine` RPC is documented in
[docs/engine.md](https://github.com/joe-broadhead/opencode-voice/blob/HEAD/docs/engine.md); it is not a Jelly `rpc`
declaration, because it is an audio contract between the host and the plugin, not a tool.

## Settings

Jelly draws a form from `jelly.contributes.settings` and writes each value into the plugin's options:

- `access` declares its three values as `choices`, with Jelly's own labels: **Allowed** (`all`, the default), **Ask
  before changes** (`ask-changes`) and **Read only** (`read-only`).
- `maxRecordSeconds` (Longest recording) is a whole number from 5 to 120, 120 by default. The engine RPC uses it too.
- `submit` and `statusIndicator` are not declared: they apply only to OpenCode's terminal UI and do nothing in Jelly,
  which runs its own dictation and shows its own listening state. They stay options in `opencode.json`.

These sets and bounds are the options parser's own, so Jelly never saves a value the plugin refuses. `voice`, `sttModel`
and `language` are not declared: the parser takes any voice or model name and any language code, so a closed set would
be narrower than what it accepts. Choices and bounds need a Jelly that includes app#1301: an older Jelly refuses a
setting that declares them. `test/unit/jelly.test.ts` checks the settings against Jelly's setting contract, restated in
`test/support/jelly-settings.ts`, and checks each declared value and bound against the options parser.

# Scripting

Every plugin of this family answers a tools RPC, `<plugin id>.tools`. Voice's is `voice.dictation.tools`: `describe`,
plus one method per known tool, with a class. A script calls a tool with **no model**, as a session and its agent.

The session is created for the script with an agent (`opencode api post /api/session -d '{"title":"…","agent":"build","location":{"directory":"/path/to/project"}}'`, with `data.id` kept). The body is
`{"input":{"sessionID":"<id>","input":{…}}}`: both keys are required, and no other key is allowed. Give the project as the session's `location`: a session made without one belongs to the service's default location, where the project's agents may not exist, and each call then fails `Agent not found`.

```sh
opencode api post /api/rpc/voice.dictation.tools/voice_speak -H "x-opencode-directory:$PWD" -d '{"input":{"sessionID":"<id>","input":{"text":"Stand-up is at nine."}}}'
```

A `voice` result comes back as `{ output?, text }`: the tool's structured content when it has any, and its text parts
joined by newlines.

`describe` lists each method's class and — with a session — the permission resolved exactly as a call would resolve it:

```sh
opencode api post /api/rpc/voice.dictation.tools/describe -H "x-opencode-directory:$PWD" -d '{"input":{"sessionID":"<id>"}}'
```

## Methods

| Method | Class | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `voice_status` | read | The engine, models, microphone and next step. |
| `voice_speak` | write | Speaks text on the machine. |

## The location

Run the command in the project whose agent you mean, and send the call to that location explicitly:

```sh
opencode api post /api/rpc/<id>/<method> -H "x-opencode-directory:$PWD" -d '{…}'
```

Without it the call goes to the service's default location and fails `rpc.unavailable` if the plugin is not loaded
there. The HTTP equivalents are the `location[directory]` query parameter and the same header. `describe` reports the
`location` that answered and a `locationHint`.

A location unloads after OpenCode's idle timeout. If a scheduled script gets `rpc.unavailable` from a location that was
loaded before, send the call again once: the request loads the location. Jobs keeps its own location loaded.

## Permissions

The rules are the agent's, then the session's, last match wins. Only an `allow` runs: an `ask` is refused with
`PERMISSION_DENIED`, with no prompt and no tool call; a `deny` is refused with no call.

**Every tool is allowed by default**, and a script gets the same default: the tools RPC resolves the rule before
dispatch, and the default allow *is* that allow. To restrict a script:

1. set the plugin's `access` option to `"ask-changes"` (speaking asks, and a script's ask is refused because no one can
   answer it) or `"read-only"` (speaking is denied);
2. give the script's agent its own `deny` rule for `voice_speak`.

A saved "Always allow" from an earlier interactive call does not authorize an ad-hoc script — a script's grant is a
rule in config, or a session whose `permissions` include it.

## Refusals

A failure is the RPC error `failed` with `data: { code, next }`. The plugin's own codes and their next steps are in
`docs/configuration.md`; the RPC's are:

| Code | When | What to do |
|---|---|---|
| `PERMISSION_DENIED` | the rule resolves to ask, or a deny hides the method | add an allow rule for the action to the session's agent or to the session |
| `SESSION_UNKNOWN` | the session is not known in this location | create the session in the location you mean, and pass its id |
| `SESSION_AGENT_REQUIRED` | the session names no agent | create a session that names an agent |
| `TOOL_UNAVAILABLE` | OpenCode does not list the method's tool now | call `describe` to see the methods there are |
| `CANCELLED` | the call was cancelled | call the method again if you still need the result |
| `UPSTREAM_ERROR` | the engine failed | its first line, redacted and cut to 300 characters, is in the message |

Upstream error text is cut to its first line, at most 300 characters, with tokens and signed URLs redacted.

## What scripts cannot do

- They cannot dictate: a microphone turn is a person's act in the terminal UI.
- They cannot transcribe a file: file transcription belongs to `utilities_speech_transcribe`.
